segments.text: Gummy pops a mint candy into his mouth.
But his mouth temperature hasn't changed one bit.
The tongue has tiny sensors that detect real cold.
Menthol from the mint binds to that same sensor.
Pressing it sends the exact same signal as real cold.
The brain just reads the signal and assumes it's cold.
Check again - the thermometer reading hasn't moved.
Menthol presses the cold sensor directly, making it feel cool.
